stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 3 x^{2} - 11 x - 1 \) and \( g(x) = x - 1 \). Find the exact total area of the regions between the graphs of f and g from \( x = -1 \) to \( x = \frac{9}{2} \).

worked_solution.text: \( f(x) - g(x) = 3 x \left(x - 4\right) \), so the graphs cross at \( x = 0 \) and \( x = 4 \), both inside the interval. f is above g before the first crossing and after the second, and below g between them.
worked_solution.rule_named: intersections and order of the curves

worked_solution.text: The pieces are \( \int_{-1}^{0} \left(f(x) - g(x)\right)\,dx = 7 \), \( \int_{0}^{4} \left(g(x) - f(x)\right)\,dx = 32 \) and \( \int_{4}^{\frac{9}{2}} \left(f(x) - g(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{13}{8} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: area of each piece, upper minus lower

worked_solution.text: The total area is the sum of the pieces, \( \frac{325}{8} \).

options.derivation: the curves split correctly but each piece integrated as lower minus upper
f(x) - g(x) integrated once over the whole interval, across both crossings
the crossing at x = 4 missed, so the second integral runs from 0 to 9/2 across it
